sections.overview: Avicularia minatrix is a South American arboreal tarantula described from Venezuela and currently accepted as a distinct species in the genus Avicularia.
sections.identification: Adults are distinguished by vivid orange lateral spots across a black abdomen; taxonomic descriptions separate it from similar Avicularia using additional anatomical characters.
sections.habitat: Verified records place the species in Venezuela and Brazil, but published locality and ecological data are too sparse to define its full habitat preferences.
sections.diet: No species-specific field diet study was located; as a tarantula, it is predatory, but prey breadth and hunting details should not be inferred from captive-care accounts.
sections.behavior: The species belongs to Avicularia, a genus of New World tarantulas; direct observations of its activity, defensive behavior and web use remain poorly documented.
sections.reproduction: The taxonomic literature recognizes both sexes and illustrates diagnostic adult structures, but the sources reviewed provide no reliable species-specific account of courtship or egg-sac care.
sections.ecology: It is closely related to other pinktoe tarantulas such as A. avicularia, but its orange abdominal spotting provides a useful distinction from that familiar relative.
sections.conservation: The World Spider Catalog confirms its accepted taxonomic status and range, but no species-level global conservation assessment or population trend was located.
